rules.title: Annual rent increase limited to CPI or 4%, whichever is less
rules.quote: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.
rules.summary: Landlords may not increase rent by more than the CPI increase over a 12-month lookback period, and the increase cannot exceed 4% in any case.
rules.coverage_text: All multiple dwellings subject to rent control
rules.exemption_note: Exemptions include public housing, hotels/motels, commercial rentals, newly constructed multiple dwellings (for up to 30 years), vacant properties rehabilitated at 50%+ of value (5 years), and substantially rehabilitated dwellings meeting requirements.
rules.penalty: Fine of not less than $100 but not exceeding $2,000 or imprisonment for not more than 90 days or both; Municipal Court may impose additional monetary penalty not to exceed $2,000 per violation.

rules.title: Only one rent increase per 12 months; increase applies regardless of tenant turnover or ownership change
rules.quote: The rents for any housing space shall not be increased more than the percentages stated above in any consecutive twelve-month period irrespective of the number of different tenants occupying the housing space during the twelve-month period, any change of ownership of the landlord or vacancy of the housing space.
rules.summary: Rent cannot be increased more than once in any 12-month period, regardless of tenant turnover or change in property ownership.
rules.coverage_text: All housing spaces subject to rent control
rules.penalty: Fine of not less than $100 but not exceeding $2,000 or imprisonment for not more than 90 days or both; Municipal Court may impose additional monetary penalty not to exceed $2,000 per violation.

rules.title: 30-day advance notice required for rent increases
rules.quote: Any landlord seeking a rental increase pursuant to this section shall give the Rent Regulation Officer and the affected tenant written notice of the proposed increase at least 30 days in advance.
rules.summary: Landlords must give tenants and the Rent Regulation Officer written notice of a proposed rent increase at least 30 days before it takes effect.
rules.coverage_text: All rent increases under rent control
rules.penalty: Fine of not less than $100 but not exceeding $2,000 or imprisonment for not more than 90 days or both; Municipal Court may impose additional monetary penalty not to exceed $2,000 per violation.

rules.title: No rent increase allowed without substantial compliance and registration
rules.quote: No annual rent increase, major new improvement surcharge, tax surcharge, or hardship increase is allowed, if the dwelling is not in substantial compliance and/or has not met registration requirements as specified in subsection 19:2-9.8.
rules.summary: Landlords cannot raise rent unless the dwelling is free from code violations and has been properly registered with the Rent Control Board.
rules.coverage_text: All dwellings subject to rent control
rules.penalty: Fine of not less than $100 but not exceeding $2,000 or imprisonment for not more than 90 days or both; Municipal Court may impose additional monetary penalty not to exceed $2,000 per violation.

rules.title: New construction exemption from rent control for up to 30 years
rules.quote: The provisions of the Rent Control Ordinance, which limit the periodic or regular increases in base rentals of dwelling units shall not apply to newly constructed multiple dwellings for a period of time not to exceed the period of amortization of any initial mortgage loan obtained for the multiple dwelling, or for 30 years following completion of construction, whichever is less.
rules.summary: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from rent increase limits for the amortization period of the initial mortgage or 30 years, whichever is shorter.
rules.exemption_note: Applies only to newly constructed multiple dwellings with Certificate of Occupancy; exemption remains with property through ownership changes.

rules.title: Vacant property exemption from rent control for 5 years after 50% rehabilitation
rules.quote: Dwellings which become vacant and remain vacant for a minimum of 18 months or dwellings which are already vacant on the effective date of this section shall be exempt for a period of five years from any restrictions in the rent that the landlord may charge, if the Rent Control Board determines that the cost of reconstruction or rehabilitation during a twelve-month period has exceeded 50% of the fair market value of the dwelling and that the dwelling has received a Certificate of Occupancy and meets all applicable State and municipal health and housing codes.
rules.summary: Dwellings vacant for at least 18 months are exempt from rent control for 5 years if rehabilitation costs exceed 50% of fair market value and the dwelling meets all codes.
rules.coverage_text: Dwellings vacant for at least 18 months and rehabilitated at 50%+ of fair market value
rules.exemption_note: Application must be submitted within 2 years of first permit; requires appraisal, Certificate of Occupancy, and sworn affidavit that prior tenants were not evicted for this purpose.

rules.title: Substantial rehabilitation exempts initial rent if costs exceed 50% of fair market value
rules.quote: Substantially reconstructed or rehabilitated dwellings shall not be restricted in initial rent charged, if the Rent Control Board has made the following determinations: a. The Board shall determine that the cost of reconstruction or rehabilitation during a twelve-month period exceeds 50% of the fair market value of the property.
rules.summary: Substantially rehabilitated dwellings may charge unrestricted initial rent if rehabilitation costs within a 12-month period exceed 50% of fair market value and all code requirements are met.
rules.exemption_note: Application must be submitted within 2 years of first permit; requires appraisal, permits, rehabilitation plan (if over 4 units), and Certificate of Occupancy.

rules.title: Cap on annual rent increase: no more than 25% in one year
rules.quote: Since an immediate rent increase of more than 25% above the prior monthly rent may be considered unconscionable and imposes a hardship on a tenant, the Rent Control Board shall not grant increases exceeding 25% in any one year for any tenant.
rules.summary: The Rent Control Board cannot grant any rent increase exceeding 25% of the prior monthly rent in any one-year period.
rules.coverage_text: All rent increases under rent control jurisdiction
rules.exemption_note: This cap applies to cumulative increases from all sources (base rent increases, major improvements, hardships) in a 12-month period.
